o1.biggest_strength: Tight, honest maths: it halves the 19-point fit-finder gap to allow for keen buyers self-selecting, and it flags that a Christmas run will distort results unless judged against a holdout.
o1.biggest_mistake: The delivered message only links to the fit finder and gives first-time bra buyers no real fit help, and it never totals what the whole plan saves.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a short post-delivery fit-check message for first-time bra buyers and a single total-savings line ranking the three fixes by money.

o2.biggest_strength: Starts from where the money sits (£139,800 of returns, £31,360 of tickets) and adds practical bra fit guidance on delivery plus a day-5 'How's the fit?' nudge, which hits the fit problem before a return is booked.
o2.biggest_mistake: The day-3 'Nearly there' message can fire before any courier scan, so the [tracking status] field may be empty or confusing. Six messages also stretches the 'short and few' principle.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Send the day-3 message only after a courier scan (warehouse check otherwise) and add a Christmas or seasonality caveat to the expected numbers.

reason: Both get the three big fixes and the maths right, but the second gives me a total saving, a pre-dispatch size check and real fit help after delivery, which is exactly where my bra returns come from.
